english: Let $X$ denote the number of successes in $5$ independent trials, each with the same probability of success $p$, where $0<p<1$. It is given that the variance of $X$ is $1.2$ and that $P(X=4)>P(X=1)$. Then the value of $\dfrac{P(X=5)}{P(X=4)}$ is ______.
hindi: माना कि $X$, $5$ स्वतन्त्र परीक्षणों में सफलताओं की संख्या है, प्रत्येक परीक्षण में सफलता की प्रायिकता समान $p$ है, जहाँ $0<p<1$ है। दिया है कि $X$ का प्रसरण $1.2$ है तथा $P(X=4)>P(X=1)$ है। तब $\dfrac{P(X=5)}{P(X=4)}$ का मान ______ है।
solution_full: $X\sim B(5,p)$ with $q=1-p$. Variance of a binomial distribution: $npq=5pq=1.2$, so $pq=0.24$, i.e. $p^{2}-p+0.24=0$, giving $p=0.6$ or $p=0.4$.

Choosing the root: $P(X=4)=\binom{5}{4}p^{4}q$ and $P(X=1)=\binom{5}{1}pq^{4}$, so $\dfrac{P(X=4)}{P(X=1)}=\left(\dfrac{p}{q}\right)^{3}$. This exceeds $1$ only if $p>q$, so $p=0.6$, $q=0.4$ (mean $3$, variance $1.2$).
originality_note: New: the binomial variance gives two symmetric values of p, and an inequality between two binomial probabilities (not the mean) selects one of them (way 5: variance of a binomial linked with comparison of binomial probabilities). Closest known: 'mean and variance of a binomial are given; find n and p'. Different because: only the variance is given, so the student must break the p, q symmetry with the probability inequality.
blueprint_concepts: Mean and variance of a binomial distribution

concept_use.Binomial probability distribution: P(X = 4)/P(X = 1) = (p/q)^3 and P(X = 5)/P(X = 4) = p/(5q) use the binomial probabilities.
concept_use.Mean and variance of a binomial distribu: The variance 5pq = 1.2 of the binomial distribution gives p = 0.6 or 0.4.
